chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was of silver. I said to him, 'Was there a stone in it?' He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What material was the Prophet's ring made of and did it have a stone?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad wearing a silver ring without an inscribed stone, a detail often discussed in contrast to later caliphal practices. It highlights the simplicity of the Prophet's adornment and serves as a basis for Shia jurists in determining the permissibility and preferred material for men's rings, emphasizing silver over gold.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan and Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was of leaf (silver)’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was there a stone in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan and Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the ring (insignia) of the Messenger of Allah, was made of leaf (dirham).’
I then asked if it had any stone, and he (the Imam) said, ‘No, it did not have a stone.’”
